title_en: Getting 5% Yield With Half the Volatility | Jeff Klingelhofer, Aristotle Pacific
title_zh: 以一半的波动获取 5% 收益 | Jeff Klingelhofer，Aristotle Pacific
subtitle_zh: Jeff Klingelhofer 谈相对价值投资、三只新固定收益 ETF 与利率展望。
description: Getting 5% Yield With Half the Volatility | Jeff Klingelhofer, Aristotle Pacific

turns.en: Welcome to Behind the Ticker, the podcast where we go beyond the symbol and into the strategy. I'm Brad Roth, founder and chief investment officer at Thor Funds, and in each episode, I sit down with ETF managers, CIOs, and industry leaders to break down how these funds are actually built, how they behave in real markets, and how advisors use them in real portfolios.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 Behind the Ticker，一档带我们穿越代码、深入策略的播客。我是 Brad Roth，Thor Funds 的创始人兼首席投资官。每一期节目，我都会和 ETF 基金经理、CIO 以及行业领袖坐下来，拆解这些基金到底是怎么构建的、在真实市场里表现如何，以及投顾在真实的投资组合里怎么使用它们。

turns.en: Most people just see a ticker symbol, but we know much more goes on behind the ticker. Hey, Jeff, welcome to the show. Hi. Excited to be here.
turns.zh: 大多数人只看到一个交易代码，但我们知道，代码背后藏着的东西要多得多。嘿，Jeff，欢迎来到节目。你好，很高兴来到这里。

turns.en: Thank you. Looking forward to a great conversation. So before we get started, why don't we give everybody a bit about your background? You started at Pemko and Newport Beach.
turns.zh: 谢谢你，我很期待这次精彩的对话。在正式开始之前，不如先给大家讲讲你的背景？你最早是在 Newport Beach 的 PIMCO 起步的。

turns.en: You've taken a couple of stops in Tokyo and London and then some years over at Thornburg. And Jen joined Aristotle in 2024, so can you walk us through that whole path?
turns.zh: 之后你在 Tokyo 和 London 都待过几站，又在 Thornburg 工作了好些年，然后在 2024 年加入了 Aristotle。能不能带我们走一遍这整段职业路径？

turns.en: Yeah. I'm happy to. I mean, you kind of nailed it. Started my career at Pemko. Didn't know a lot about the world of fixed income. It's one of those things that some folks want to go into investing, but not many folks dream of being a bond investor, and so that was really my first foray, and it was fantastic.
turns.zh: 好啊，我很乐意。你基本上说对了。我的职业生涯始于 PIMCO，当时对固定收益（fixed income）这个世界了解不多。有些人想进入投资行业，但很少有人梦想成为一名债券投资者，所以那其实是我第一次涉足这个领域，而且感觉非常棒。

turns.en: It really exposed me to a lot of very, very smart people that cared a lot about their career and gave me a great background. But like a lot of people that go into the role of finance, you kind of want to move from a more back office role into a little bit more of a front office role.
turns.zh: 它真的让我接触到非常多非常聪明、对自己事业极其上心的人，也给了我一个很好的底子。但和很多进入金融行业的人一样，你会想从偏后台（back office）的岗位，慢慢往前台（front office）的岗位挪。

turns.en: So I had the opportunity to begin doing that. My career was in risk at that moment and exported a risk function from the Newport Beach office at Pemko to Tokyo and then ultimately to London and then decided I wanted to make my way to an MBA program.
turns.zh: 所以我有机会开始这么做。那时候我做的是风险（risk）相关工作，把 PIMCO Newport Beach 办公室的一套风险职能输出到了 Tokyo，之后又带到了 London，然后我就决定要去读一个 MBA 项目。

turns.en: So I went to University of Chicago and got my MBA. And if I'm being honest, I probably would have said at that time I thought I would end up back at a Pemko or a BlackRock.
turns.zh: 于是我去了 University of Chicago 读完了 MBA。说实话，那时候我大概会说，我以为自己最终会回到 PIMCO 或者 BlackRock 这样的地方。

turns.en: One of the really large firms of the world, quite a lot of prestige come along with those, but I did something a little bit different over my summer internship and just picked a really small hedge fund and worked there.
turns.zh: 就是世界上那种超大型机构，自带相当多的光环。但我在暑期实习时做了个不太一样的选择——挑了一家非常小的对冲基金去工作。

turns.en: And I remember walking in on day one and they just said, hey, Jeff, welcome to the team. It's five of us. Go find interesting things. And I was just like, what do you mean?
turns.zh: 我记得第一天走进去，他们就直接说：嘿 Jeff，欢迎加入团队，我们就五个人，你去找点有意思的东西吧。我当时就愣了：你什么意思？

turns.en: Like direct me a little bit more, but there's like, look, the world's your oyster. Just go see what you can do and find something interesting.
turns.zh: 就是能不能多给我点方向，但他们的意思是：看，世界任你遨游，你就去看看自己能做点什么，找点有意思的东西出来。

turns.en: And so that really changed my path as I looked forward. I wanted to be part of a small entrepreneurial team and ultimately joined Thornburg.
turns.zh: 这件事真的改变了我往后的道路。我想成为一支小而具创业精神团队的一员，最终加入了 Thornburg。

turns.en: It was a very well-established company, but fixed income was a smaller part of it. So I was employee number three on the tax well fixed income side and just really grew it from there.
turns.zh: 那是一家非常成熟的公司，但固定收益只是其中较小的一块。所以在应税固定收益（taxable fixed income）这边，我是第三号员工，然后就从那里一点点把它做大。

turns.en: So ultimately I became a portfolio manager on all their strategies and was head of investments for about the first, last four or five years of my career and then decided that I wanted to get back home to Newport Beach, which is kind of where my family is and where I grew up in Southern California.
turns.zh: 最终我成了他们所有策略的组合经理，并在职业生涯的最后四五年里担任投资主管。之后我决定回到 Newport Beach 的老家——我的家人就在那儿，我也是在南加州长大的。

turns.en: So yeah, you're right. I've been with Aristotle here for the last couple of years, just an incredible team and incredible fit and alignment with my background of what we'll talk about, I'm sure, and relative value investing.
turns.zh: 所以，是的，你说得对。过去这几年我一直在 Aristotle，这是一支非常出色的团队，和我的背景也极其契合、高度一致——我相信我们待会儿会聊到，还有相对价值（relative value）投资。

turns.en: Yeah, we're definitely going to get into that, but I always have to ask people before we talk business, any hobbies, what do you like to do when you're outside of work?
turns.zh: 对，我们肯定会聊到那个。不过在谈正事之前，我总得先问问大家：有什么爱好吗？工作之外你喜欢做点什么？

turns.en: Well, I love the ocean. I'd like to say I'm a great surfer. I'm a horrible surfer, but I literally get angry if my feet don't touch the water or the sand at least a couple of times a week.
turns.zh: 嗯，我热爱大海。我真想说我是个冲浪高手，其实我冲浪烂透了。但只要有一周哪怕几次脚没沾到海水或者沙滩，我是真的会生气。

turns.en: So that was a little bit tougher being in Santa Fe, New Mexico and Thorbrick. So excited to be back. My real passion, I would say is sailing.
turns.zh: 所以之前待在 New Mexico 的 Santa Fe、在 Thornburg 那会儿就有点难熬。因此我很高兴能回来。要说我真正的热情，那应该是帆船。

turns.en: So I'm a sailor. I play tennis. Those are my two things and then family as well, just keeps me busy on the day to day. But yeah, swimming, sailing, tennis, those are the big things.
turns.zh: 所以我玩帆船，也打网球，这是我的两样爱好，再加上家庭，日常就把我忙得团团转。总之，游泳、帆船、网球，这些是我的大头。

turns.en: Love it. It's so funny, every time I talk to somebody on, you know, I'm over in Pittsburgh, every time I talk to somebody who's in that Newport Beach, California area, they're always, it's the same hobbies.
turns.zh: 太好了。有意思的是，你知道，我人在 Pittsburgh，每次我跟在加州 Newport Beach 那一带的人聊天，他们的爱好永远都是那几样。

turns.en: It's like, I love the beach. And I'm over here, like I got to grind six months through winter while you guys go sailing. Yeah, it comes with its own costs, right?
turns.zh: 就好像——我爱海滩。可我在这边，得熬过整整六个月的冬天，而你们却在那儿扬帆出海。是啊，这也是有代价的，对吧？

turns.en: And literally some of the cost side of things. And so I feel like there's no reason to be here if you're not going to connect with the water.
turns.zh: 而且实打实地说，也确实有成本这一面。所以我觉得，如果你不去亲近这片水域，那就没什么理由待在这儿了。

turns.en: And so I think you've just got a natural selection. A lot of folks just naturally would gravitate towards the beach, the ocean, being outdoors because you pay the price in terms of housing.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得这其实是一种自然选择。很多人自然而然就会被海滩、大海、户外活动吸引，因为你在房价上是付出了代价的。

turns.en: So you kind of got to get out of the smaller house occasionally and just take advantage of what you got. Love it. So let's talk about Aristotle funds.
turns.zh: 所以你总得时不时从那栋小房子里出来，好好利用你拥有的东西。太好了。那我们来聊聊 Aristotle 的基金吧。

turns.en: The firm has 16 billion across mutual fund lineup in July 30th of this year. You guys launched your first three ETFs. So can you give us just a quick high level of Aristotle and what got the firm into the ETF wrapper now at this stage?
turns.zh: 公司整个共同基金（mutual fund）产品线管理着 160 亿美元，而就在今年 7 月 30 日，你们推出了头三只 ETF。能不能先给我们一个大致的介绍，讲讲 Aristotle 是什么，以及为什么公司在这个阶段选择进入 ETF 这个外壳（wrapper）？

turns.en: Yeah, so Aristotle has been around for a decade and a half really at this point or really two decades. And so the name changed a little bit ago, but it was prior known as Pacific Asset Management.
turns.zh: 好的。到现在为止，Aristotle 其实已经有十五年、甚至差不多二十年的历史了。名字是不久前才改的，它之前叫 Pacific Asset Management。

turns.en: So it was under the guise of Pacific Life. So the team really has been together since about 2007 or even before, but it was incepted in 2007 for all intents and purposes.
turns.zh: 当时它挂在 Pacific Life 名下。所以这支团队其实大约从 2007 年、甚至更早就在一起了，不过实际上公司是在 2007 年正式成立的。

turns.en: And eventually it made its way under the Aristotle Capital brand. So Pacific Life also started PIMCO, which is where I started that they've got a pretty good heritage of launching some pretty great firms, but eventually many of them do move on.
turns.zh: 后来它归入了 Aristotle Capital 这个品牌之下。Pacific Life 还创立了 PIMCO——我就是从那儿起步的——所以他们在孵化出一些非常出色的公司方面有着相当不错的传统，只不过这些公司最终很多都会独立出去。

turns.en: And so there's been a long rich history of really the philosophy of the firm, which is looking to capture relative value across the credit spectrum.
turns.zh: 所以公司的这套投资理念有着悠久而丰富的历史，那就是在整个信用（credit）谱系里去寻找并捕捉相对价值。

turns.en: And so our four A&E ETFs, honestly, it's nothing magical that the world has been moving towards the ETF side for quite some time. They're not new products, but we really wanted to be very thoughtful about how we rolled them out to our audience.
turns.zh: 至于我们这几只 ETF，说实话并没有什么神奇的——全世界往 ETF 这一侧转移已经有一段时间了。它们并不是新产品，但我们确实想非常审慎地考虑该以什么方式把它们推向我们的受众。

turns.en: And so a lot of it was just kind of waiting and watching what our clients wanted, how they consumed them, how we thought that we could bring our unique flavor into that product.
turns.zh: 所以很大程度上就是在等待和观察：我们的客户想要什么、他们怎么使用这些产品，以及我们怎样才能把自己独特的风格融入到这类产品里。

turns.en: And so ultimately we decided to launch with a suite of outcome-oriented products on our multi-sector fixed income suite. And so they really take all that same application.
turns.zh: 最终我们决定，以我们多板块（multi-sector）固定收益产品线为基础，推出一系列以结果为导向（outcome-oriented）的产品。它们其实沿用的都是同一套方法。

turns.en: Now there are nuances, but really focusing on that relative value side, but there's nothing magical about why now or why the ETF wrapper beyond, we want to meet our clients where they are.
turns.zh: 当然其中有些细微差别，但核心还是聚焦在相对价值这一面。至于为什么是现在、为什么用 ETF 这个外壳，并没有什么玄机，无非就是我们想在客户所在的地方去迎接他们。

turns.en: And we feel like this is a great foray and ability for us to take what we've been doing and just apply it in a slightly different wrapper to meet our clients in a nuanced way.
turns.zh: 我们觉得，这是一个很好的切入点和契机，让我们把一直在做的事情，用稍微不同一点的外壳来落地，以一种更细致的方式去契合我们的客户。

turns.en: Well, let's get into the funds. I mean, like I said, you launched three fixed income ETFs, ARCP, which is your core plus, ARMS, which is your multi-sector income, and SDUR, which is your short-term income fund.
turns.zh: 好，那我们来具体聊聊这几只基金。就像我说的，你们推出了三只固定收益 ETF：ARCP，也就是你们的 Core Plus；ARMS，是你们的多板块收益（multi-sector income）；还有 SDUR，是你们的短期收益基金。

turns.en: Start us off with a big picture. What does this suite give investors? And like, why launch all three together? Yeah. Well, again, I think a lot of this is every firm has its own unique flavor, right?
turns.zh: 先从大局讲起吧。这一系列产品能给投资者带来什么？为什么三只一起推出？嗯，我觉得这在很大程度上是因为，每家公司都有自己独特的风格，对吧？

turns.en: When clients are speaking with managers or doing due diligence, I think it's really incumbent on the manager to explain not just why they're going to return good performance.
turns.zh: 当客户跟基金经理交谈、做尽职调查（due diligence）的时候，我认为经理真正有责任去解释的，不只是他们为什么能带来好的业绩。

turns.en: That's what everyone is after. But to me, it's much more about the how, right? What specifically are we trying to access? In what way? How is our team oriented?
turns.zh: 业绩是所有人都在追求的东西。但对我来说，更重要的其实是‘怎么做’，对吧？我们具体想去获取什么？以什么方式？我们团队是怎么组织的？

turns.en: How do we train people? How do we compensate them and motivate them? And all trying to look at the world in a slightly nuanced way, because there's lots of firms out there, and there's lots of good firms out there, and there's no one single way of being successful.
turns.zh: 我们怎么培养人？怎么给他们薪酬、激励他们？所有这些都是在尝试用一种更细致的方式去看这个世界，因为市面上公司很多，优秀的公司也很多，而成功并没有唯一的一条路。

turns.en: And so really the way that I would talk about it is the multi-sector fixed income side, you can think about Aristotle and kind of two quasi-distinct ARMS.
turns.zh: 所以我会这么来讲：在多板块固定收益这一块，你可以把 Aristotle 大致看成有两条相对独立、又彼此关联的业务分支（arms）。

turns.en: Now, both of them access that relative value perspective, but when you do it within a single silo part of fixed income, just bank loans, for instance, just corporates, just securitized or CLOs, it's a little bit different in how you apply that relative value lens versus the multi-sector lens.
turns.zh: 这两条都用到了相对价值的视角，但当你只在固定收益的某一个单独的‘竖井’（silo）里去做时——比如只做银行贷款、只做公司债、只做证券化产品或 CLO——你运用相对价值这套视角的方式，跟用多板块视角去比，就会有点不一样。

turns.en: And so all three of these products that Esther, ARCP, and ARMS look a lot like many of the mutual funds that we've had in our multi-sector suite for quite some time.
turns.zh: 所以这三只产品——SDUR、ARCP 和 ARMS——看起来很像是我们在多板块产品线里已经运作了相当长时间的那些共同基金。

turns.en: And really the crux of them is accessing what I will argue is a very inefficient market because of the way that many firms have what I believe to be an old construct of looking only at the individual silos within the context of multi-sector.
turns.zh: 它们真正的关键，在于去获取一个我认为非常低效的市场——之所以低效，是因为很多公司用的还是我认为是过时的一套架构：在多板块的背景下，却只盯着一个个独立的竖井去看。

turns.en: And so many firms are still set up to invest under a low tracking error, just benchmark centric approach. And all of these products represent what I will talk about as being a suite of outcomes.
turns.zh: 所以很多公司仍然是按照低跟踪误差（tracking error）、纯粹以基准（benchmark）为中心的方式来做投资。而我这几只产品代表的，是我所说的‘一整套结果’（a suite of outcomes）。

turns.en: And to me, that's what clients really should care about. They want a product to do something specific. They know when it's going to do well.
turns.zh: 在我看来，这才是客户真正应该关心的东西。他们希望一个产品去完成某件具体的事：知道它什么时候会表现好，

turns.en: They know when it may do less well. And that's okay because they know how it fits into the context of their portfolio. So really the way I would think about this suite of products is we have a little bit from left to right on the duration spectrum.
turns.zh: 也知道它什么时候可能表现差一些。这没关系，因为他们清楚它在自己的组合里是怎么契合的。所以我看待这一系列产品的方式是：在久期（duration）谱系上，我们从左到右都覆盖了一些，

turns.en: How much interest rate exposure do you want, as well as up and down on the credit spectrum? How much risk are you willing to take in pursuit of a different outcome and different return goals?
turns.zh: 也就是你想要多少利率敞口；同时在信用谱系上从上到下也都有——为了追求不同的结果和不同的回报目标，你愿意承担多少风险？

turns.en: So at the heart of all three of these funds is a relative value process, like a bottom up credit research combined with top down positioning.
turns.zh: 所以这三只基金的核心，都是一套相对价值的流程，也就是自下而上（bottom-up）的信用研究，结合自上而下（top-down）的仓位布局。

turns.en: Can you walk us through what relative value actually means in a fixed income wrapper and how your team actually implements that? Yeah, it's something I'm passionate about.
turns.zh: 能不能带我们理解一下，在固定收益这个框架里，相对价值到底是什么意思，你们团队又是怎么落地的？好，这可是我很有热情的话题。

turns.en: So I'll give an example here in a second, but let me first answer the question and then hopefully I can bring it to life and something that really matters.
turns.zh: 我马上会举一个例子，不过先让我回答这个问题，然后希望我能把它讲得活灵活现、讲出它真正的分量。

turns.en: So to me, relative value is the world of fixed income is all about income. It's all about yield. And so you can think about a suite. In today's fixed income world, bonds can range anywhere from three and a half, four-ish type percent yields all the way to low to mid-teens on the riskier side of things.
turns.zh: 对我来说，相对价值——固定收益这个世界，讲的就是收益（income），讲的就是收益率（yield）。你可以把它想成一个谱系：在今天的固定收益世界里，债券的收益率可以从大约 3.5%、4% 这种水平，一直延伸到风险更高的那一端、十几个百分点偏低的区间（low to mid-teens）。

turns.en: And so if I want to access, let's just say five percent, just doesn't matter, pick a number, but five percent. I will argue that there are lots of ways to get five percent and there is the one with the lowest potential volatility.
turns.zh: 所以如果我想获取——就说 5% 吧，具体数字不重要，随便挑一个，就 5%。我会说，拿到 5% 的方式有很多种，而其中有一种是潜在波动率最低的。

turns.en: This is an asset class that is usually meant to be less interesting, just more day to day, a little bit more balanced to an investor's portfolio.
turns.zh: 固定收益本来就是一个通常被认为‘不那么刺激’的资产类别，更偏日常，给投资者的组合多添一份平衡。

turns.en: And so the way I like to talk about it is much of the world of fixed income approaches it from a, how do I get a lot of additional yield, a lot of additional return and be willing to accept just a little bit of additional risk along with that?
turns.zh: 所以我喜欢这么讲：固定收益领域里很多人是从这个角度出发的——我怎样才能拿到更多的额外收益、更多额外回报，同时只愿意为此多承担一点点额外风险？

turns.en: And at the security level, I think that's the wrong approach. So relative value to me is almost the exact opposite. How do I get that yield target that I'm after and use the world of relative value to take potential volatility out from that actual investment?
turns.zh: 而在个券（security）层面，我认为这是错误的思路。所以对我来说，相对价值几乎是完全相反的：我怎样才能拿到我想要的那个收益率目标，同时用相对价值这套方法，把这笔投资里潜在的波动给剔除掉？

turns.en: And the reason why I think that exists, and so now I'll come to an example, is because, again, the world likes to think about the broad array of fixed income as almost distinctly different asset classes.
turns.zh: 而我认为之所以会有这种机会——那现在我来讲个例子——还是因为，市场总喜欢把固定收益这宽广的一大片，想成是几乎彼此完全不同的资产类别。

turns.en: And so if you walk into many investment teams, what you will see is a distinct asset-backed desk, a distinct CLO desk, a distinct investment-grade corporate desk, a distinct high-yield corporate desk, a distinct bank loan desk, treasury desk and on down the line.
turns.zh: 所以如果你走进很多投资团队，你会看到：一个独立的资产支持证券（asset-backed）台子，一个独立的 CLO 台子，一个独立的投资级公司债台子，一个独立的高收益公司债台子，一个独立的银行贷款台子，一个国债台子，等等一路排下去。

turns.en: And every one of them is tasked with looking within that realm to find good value. But the question becomes, who's looking across those individual desks?
turns.zh: 而每一个台子的任务，都是在自己那一亩三分地里去找好的价值。但问题就来了：谁在跨越这些独立的台子去看全局？

turns.en: And so I think the world is just wrong in the sense that it tends to think about fundamentals and valuations as two separate parts of the investment structure.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得市场在这一点上是错的：它往往把基本面（fundamentals）和估值（valuations）当成投资架构里两个彼此分离的部分。

turns.en: And so we try and keep those married throughout. Now, let me give you one example of how this really kind of came to play. So this is a very vulnerable time period, but it's just such a stark example that I love going to it.
turns.zh: 而我们则努力让这两者始终‘结为一体’。来，我给你举一个例子，说明这在现实中是怎么上演的。那是一段非常敏感的时期，但这个例子实在太鲜明了，我很喜欢拿它来说事。

turns.en: So if you think about February of 2020, COVID was all over the front page of the Wall Street Journal of New York Times. Everybody knew about COVID, but the world wasn't scared of COVID yet, right?
turns.zh: 你想一下 2020 年 2 月，那时候新冠疫情已经铺满了《华尔街日报》和《纽约时报》的头版。每个人都知道新冠，但市场还不害怕新冠，对吧？

turns.en: The markets were doing just fine. And so in mid-February, you had American Airlines, which is a large global air carrier, right? It's a brand new five-year corporate high-yield bond at 3.75%.
turns.zh: 市场一切都还好。就在 2 月中旬，American Airlines——一家大型全球航空公司——发行了一只全新的五年期公司高收益债，票息 3.75%。

turns.en: And so on that day, mid-February, the market said, issue our American Airlines 10 or five years, 3.75%. That is the going rate for that amount of risk.
turns.zh: 所以在 2 月中旬那一天，市场等于是说：American Airlines 发五年期债，3.75%，这就是承担这么多风险的通行价格。

turns.en: And on that same day, you could go access American Airlines five-year debt, 3.75%, roughly in a slightly different form. And think about this as basically secured financing.
turns.zh: 而就在那同一天，你也可以用大致相同的条件、稍微不同的形式，去获取 American Airlines 的五年期、3.75% 的债务。你可以把它理解成基本上是有抵押的融资（secured financing）。

turns.en: So it trades more like an asset-backed. It's called a WETC, Enhanced Equipment Trust Certificate. I won't get too far into the weeds, but basically when you step on an airplane, there's a good chance that airline doesn't own the aircraft.
turns.zh: 所以它的交易方式更像资产支持证券。它叫 EETC，也就是增强型设备信托证书（Enhanced Equipment Trust Certificate）。我就不钻太细了，但基本上，当你登上一架飞机时，很可能这家航空公司并不拥有这架飞机。

turns.en: What they do is they buy a bunch of aircraft, they put it in this special-purpose vehicle off balance sheet, and so long as they make lease payments to that, they have the right to fly that aircraft.
turns.zh: 他们做的是：买一批飞机，装进一个表外的特殊目的载体（special-purpose vehicle），只要他们按期向这个载体支付租金，就有权运营这些飞机。

turns.en: So February, market said, same issuer, same tender, same yield, same risk, same thing. Well, fast forward to March. Now the world is afraid of COVID.
turns.zh: 所以 2 月的时候，市场说的是：同一个发行人、同样的期限（tenor）、同样的收益率、同样的风险、同样的东西。好，快进到 3 月，这时全世界开始害怕新冠了。

turns.en: And that corporate bond that priced just a month prior in February is now trading at $0.27 on the dollar. That WETC, still not a good investment, but it's trading at $0.65 on the dollar.
turns.zh: 那只一个月前、也就是 2 月才定价的公司债，如今成交价跌到了面值的 0.27 美元。而那只 EETC——虽然也算不上好投资——但它的成交价是面值的 0.65 美元。

turns.en: And so all of a sudden, the market said, same issuer, same tender, same yield, same risk. One month later, they say, well, one is worth more than double what the other one is worth.
turns.zh: 于是突然之间，市场又说了：同一个发行人、同样的期限、同样的收益率、同样的风险。可一个月之后，他们却说：其中一个的价值是另一个的两倍还多。

turns.en: And why? My argument would be because two different people sitting on two different desks, maybe at two different offices on two separate continents, looked at those in isolation.
turns.zh: 为什么会这样？我的观点是：因为两个坐在不同台子上的人，也许在两大洲的两个不同办公室里，是孤立地去看这两样东西的。

turns.en: And it wasn't that they missed that understanding of what each one had and what didn't. It was because generally, the top-level portfolio manager, a CIO, an investment committee, they just allocate capital to those individual silos.
turns.zh: 这并不是说他们没搞清楚每一样各自有什么、缺什么，而是因为一般来说，顶层的组合经理、CIO、投资委员会，他们只是把资本分配给那些各自独立的竖井。

turns.en: Maybe they said, we think corporates are more interesting, so here you go. And so really the crux of it is we try and keep that decision married throughout the investment process.
turns.zh: 也许他们会说：我们觉得公司债更有意思，那就给你多分点。所以真正的关键在于，我们努力让这个决策在整个投资流程里始终‘结为一体’。

turns.en: And that takes place, maybe just to give one more example, and today, data centers are all over the news. We all know they're borrowing, and they're issuing debt in asset-backed form, CMBS form, investment-grade corporate form, high-yield corporate form, bank loans, private credit.
turns.zh: 这一点体现在——再举一个例子吧。今天数据中心（data centers）满天飞地上新闻。我们都知道它们在借钱，而且是以资产支持证券、CMBS、投资级公司债、高收益公司债、银行贷款、私募信贷（private credit）等各种形式发债。

turns.en: They're very thoughtful about how they raise capital, but we on the investment side, I think as a broad industry, haven't adapted to the way the world works today.
turns.zh: 它们在如何融资这件事上想得非常周全，但我们在投资这一侧——我觉得整个行业——还没有适应今天这个世界的运行方式。

turns.en: And so that really is the crux of that relative value is finding ways to keep that yield at a similar level, but take out a lot of potential volatility for the various states of the market and future times.
turns.zh: 所以，相对价值真正的核心，就是想办法把收益率维持在相近的水平，同时针对市场的各种状态和未来时段，剔除掉大量潜在的波动。

turns.en: Well, let's get into the funds specifically themselves and how this process can apply to each one. So let's start with ARCP, which is your CorePlus income.
turns.zh: 好，那我们来具体聊聊这几只基金本身，以及这套流程如何应用到每一只上。先从 ARCP 说起吧，也就是你们的 Core Plus 收益基金。

turns.en: This is designed to deliver excess return over CoreBonds with minimal added volatility. So what is CorePlus actually doing, and how does ARCP compete with names like the Ag or your former PIMCO CorePlus fund?
turns.zh: 它的设计目标，是在核心债券（core bonds）之上获取超额收益，同时把额外增加的波动降到最低。那么 Core Plus 到底在做什么？ARCP 又要怎么跟像 AGG、或者你以前在 PIMCO 的那只 Core Plus 基金这样的名字竞争？

turns.en: Well, so you bring up an interesting kind of point, kind of that active passive debate, if it's just the Ag, and of course, very much an active manager who's right up the street from us with the PIMCO side.
turns.zh: 嗯，你提到了一个很有意思的点，其实就是那个主动与被动的争论——一边是 AGG，另一边当然是一家非常主动的管理人，也就是就在我们街对面的 PIMCO。

turns.en: And I'll talk about them a little bit differently, because I really do think that they serve a different place in investors' portfolios. You know, I think the Ag is a very inexpensive product, and so the biggest benefit is you're not paying a manager to generate those returns.
turns.zh: 我会把它们分开来讲，因为我确实认为它们在投资者的组合里扮演着不同的角色。你知道，我觉得 AGG 是一只非常便宜的产品，所以它最大的好处就是：你不用付钱给经理去获取那些回报。

turns.en: And what the Ag is after, and we have to always keep in mind, it's not after anything in particular, right? It's not after income. It's not after a certain interest rate exposure or quality exposure or anything.
turns.zh: 而且要始终记住，AGG 追求的东西——它其实并不特别追求什么，对吧？它不追求收益，也不追求某种特定的利率敞口、或质量敞口，什么都不追求。

turns.en: It's just a set of rules that define what the benchmark is, and then they're just trying to mimic that benchmark. And so its duration can move all over the place, and it's gone from four to six over the last decade.
turns.zh: 它只是一套定义了基准是什么的规则，然后就是努力去复制那个基准。所以它的久期可以到处飘——过去十年里就从 4 变到了 6。

turns.en: The quality component has come way down as the treasury and Fed are buying treasuries or terming out debt or engaging in operation twists, things change.
turns.zh: 它的质量构成也大幅下降了，因为财政部和美联储在买国债、在把债务期限拉长、或者在做扭转操作（Operation Twist），情况一直在变。

turns.en: And so it's not after an outcome, but it's great if you just want a go-to bond that looks like the Ag, and you accept that it doesn't have your end goals in mind along with it.
turns.zh: 所以它并不追求某个结果。但如果你就是想要一只看起来像 AGG 那样的、随手可得的债券，并且能接受它并没有把你的最终目标放在心上，那它也挺好的。

turns.en: So I think active manager has a place to play, regardless, just because we are after an outcome. I am very cognizant of the difference between a duration of four and six and how quality shifts and relative value shifts.
turns.zh: 所以我认为主动管理人无论如何都有一席之地，就因为我们是在追求一个结果。我非常清楚久期 4 和 6 之间的差别，也清楚质量如何变化、相对价值如何变化。

turns.en: So that would be kind of the biggest thing, but the way I think about the Ag is just core plus bonds and the Ag included within that is its outcome is meant to be kind of a teeter totter of both things.
turns.zh: 这大概就是最大的区别。不过我看待 AGG 的方式，就是把它归到‘核心加债券’（core plus bonds）里，而 AGG 包含在其中，它的结果本来就该是两样东西的一个‘跷跷板’平衡。

turns.en: Clients generally want an interesting level of income, an interesting level of total return, and they also want right along with that balance to their portfolio, right?
turns.zh: 客户通常想要一个有吸引力的收益水平、一个有吸引力的总回报水平，同时还想让组合有一份平衡，对吧？

turns.en: It's meant to be a low volatility investment, ideally in many times the value of it will actually go up as the value of equities go down in a recession, let's say.
turns.zh: 它本该是一项低波动的投资，理想情况下，很多时候——比如说在一场衰退中——当股票的价值下跌时，它的价值反而会上涨。

turns.en: And so that's really what we're trying to accomplish with it. We're trying to say, all right, you have an Ag in mind. We're trying to outperform that by 100 to 150 basis points throughout a cycle.
turns.zh: 所以这正是我们想通过它达成的目标。我们想说的是：好，你心里有一只 AGG，那我们就试着在整个周期里跑赢它 100 到 150 个基点（basis points）。

turns.en: We've delivered well more than that for other very similar products. And we don't think we have to give you a whole lot of additional volatility in order to achieve that outcome.
turns.zh: 在其他一些非常类似的产品上，我们交付的远远不止这个数。而且我们认为，要实现这个结果，并不需要让你多承担很多额外的波动。

turns.en: And so that application of how we look at the world would be very different than the application of how PIMCO looks at the world. A lot of fixed income managers like to start from the top down.
turns.zh: 所以我们这套看待世界的方式，跟 PIMCO 看待世界的方式会很不一样。很多固定收益经理喜欢从自上而下入手。

turns.en: What's the Fed going to do? Are we going to be in a recession in 26 or 27? What might be happening with oil and the war in Russia, Ukraine and all of these things?
turns.zh: 美联储会怎么做？我们会在 2026 或 2027 年陷入衰退吗？石油、俄乌战争这些事可能会怎么发展？

turns.en: And that's OK if you believe that they have a leg up on doing that and that's part of their process. But we're going to approach the world from a very different perspective, right?
turns.zh: 如果你相信他们在这件事上有优势、而且这是他们流程的一部分，那也没问题。但我们看待世界的方式会非常不同，对吧？

turns.en: What are the individual companies doing? What are consumers telling us and where can we access those individual balance sheets, whether they be a consumer balance sheet, a corporate balance sheet, a government balance sheet in a nuanced way to deliver that return, but hopefully with a lot less volatility than its yield might suggest?
turns.zh: 我们会问：一家家公司在做什么？消费者在告诉我们什么？我们又能从哪里去触及这些个别的资产负债表——不管是消费者、企业还是政府的资产负债表——以一种细致的方式去交付那份回报，同时又希望波动比它的收益率所暗示的要小得多？

turns.en: So taking a look at arms, which is the multi sector, first like quick question, biggest difference between core and multi sector, just you can go more places.
turns.zh: 那来看看 ARMS，也就是多板块那只。先问个快问题：core 和 multi-sector 之间最大的区别，是不是就是你能去的地方更多？

turns.en: That's the biggest thing, right? So we start with core, which is kind of investment grade only. And then our core plus strategy, which is also very similar to many other, you start introducing the ability to buy in the high yield market, the below investment grade site, but not too much, right?
turns.zh: 这就是最大的区别，对吧？我们从 core 开始，它基本上只投投资级（investment grade）。然后是 core plus 策略——这也和很多其他产品很类似——你开始引入在高收益市场、也就是投资级以下那一侧买入的能力，但不会买太多，对吧？

turns.en: You still want it to be just that ballast. When you move to the world of multi sector, arms, strategic type products, you really open up that box.
turns.zh: 你仍然希望它只是那份‘压舱石’。而当你转到多板块的世界——ARMS 这类 strategic 型产品——你就真的把那个盒子打开了。

turns.en: And so the traditional multi sector portfolio is 60 percent investment grade, 40 percent below investment grade, and that's very similar to our arms products.
turns.zh: 传统的多板块组合是 60% 投资级、40% 投资级以下，这和我们的 ARMS 产品非常相似。

turns.en: But what you get for that is instead of just beating the egg by 100 to 150 basis points throughout a cycle, now we're targeting 250 basis points, right?
turns.zh: 但你由此换来的，是不再只是在整个周期里跑赢 AGG 100 到 150 个基点，而是把目标定在了 250 个基点，对吧？

turns.en: Two and a half percent. And so for clients that are saying, great, I've got my fixed income allocation, or maybe I don't need a core core plus product in my portfolio.
turns.zh: 也就是 2.5%。所以对于那些会说‘好，我已经有固定收益配置了’，或者‘也许我组合里不需要一个 core / core plus 产品’的客户来说，

turns.en: I want something more interesting, a higher level of yield and total return, but I still don't want the volatility of equities or private credit or private equity, right?
turns.zh: ‘我想要更有意思一点的东西、更高的收益率和总回报，但我又不想要股票、私募信贷或私募股权那样的波动’，对吧？

turns.en: That's kind of that next step out. So it's a different return target and investors accepting also along with that a little bit higher volatility versus a core core plus product.
turns.zh: 这就是往外迈的下一步。所以它是一个不同的回报目标，投资者也随之接受比 core / core plus 产品稍高一点的波动。

turns.en: So just curious, like how much flexibility the team has there in terms of being able to go anywhere, or do you have to keep a certain amount of exposures in certain parts of the market, like investment grade, high yield or floating rate?
turns.zh: 我有点好奇，团队在那方面有多大灵活性——是可以到处去投，还是说你们必须在市场的某些部分保留一定量的敞口，比如投资级、高收益或浮动利率（floating rate）？

turns.en: Or is it just, hey, this is where our team sees opportunity, this is the direction we're going to go, or does it stay fairly diversified? It will always stay fairly diversified, but right along with that, there is a lot of flexibility to ourselves and many managers in how they can migrate all of those different asset classes.
turns.zh: 还是说就是‘嘿，我们团队在哪里看到机会，就往哪个方向走’？它会一直保持相当分散吗？它会始终保持相当分散，但与此同时，无论是我们自己还是很多管理人，在这些不同资产类别之间如何迁移，都有很大的灵活性。

turns.en: And so I'll go back to something I said earlier. I think it's really incumbent for the end user or their advisors to make sure they understand where, how and why a manager might pull those individual levers.
turns.zh: 所以我要回到我前面说过的一点。我认为，最终用户或者他们的投顾，真的有责任去搞清楚：一位经理可能会在什么时候、以什么方式、出于什么原因去拉动那些个别的杠杆。

turns.en: And so, you know, in something like ARMS, we can have as little as 25% below investment grade, right? And we can have up to mid 60 type percent investment grade.
turns.zh: 所以在像 ARMS 这样的产品里，我们投资级以下的部分可以低到只有 25%，对吧？而投资级的部分可以高到 60% 出头的水平。

turns.en: And so we really want to be very cognizant of where and how we might pull that lever because in just a very broad brush, the world of high quality versus low quality at times, you may be paid to take that lower quality risk.
turns.zh: 所以我们真的想非常清楚，我们会在什么时候、以什么方式去拉动那个杠杆。因为粗略地讲，在高质量与低质量这个世界里，有时候你承担那份更低质量的风险是能得到补偿的。

turns.en: I would argue today you're not being well paid. And so we don't want a whole lot of it. And so we are very much on the low end of that range.
turns.zh: 而我会说，今天你得到的补偿并不划算。所以我们不想持有太多这类东西，我们目前处在那个区间的很低端。

turns.en: But I'll also go back. It's not just as nuanced or I shouldn't even say it's not even just as simple as saying, well, how much is investment grade and how much is below investment grade?
turns.zh: 但我还要退一步说：这件事并不只是‘多少是投资级、多少是投资级以下’这么简单。

turns.en: Because there might be time periods where agency mortgages look tremendously interesting versus corporates. And agency mortgages are backed by the government.
turns.zh: 因为可能会有一些时期，机构抵押贷款（agency mortgages）相比公司债看起来极具吸引力。而机构抵押贷款是有政府背书的，

turns.en: So the default risk is de minimis to zero. We can debate that, but very, very low, right? You're getting a very different risk. I always talk about bonds as we'd like to talk about them as distinct things in different wrappers and different terminology.
turns.zh: 所以违约风险小到几乎为零。这一点我们可以争论，但确实非常非常低，对吧？你面对的是很不一样的风险。我总是说，我们喜欢把债券当成不同的东西来谈——用不同的外壳、不同的术语。

turns.en: But at the end of the day, how much cash am I going to get? When am I going to get it? And how likely am I to get it? So just timing, probability and quantity of cash flows.
turns.zh: 但归根结底，无非是：我能拿到多少现金？什么时候拿到？拿到的可能性有多大？也就是现金流的时间、概率和数量。

turns.en: And all of a sudden it's just a bond, right? Doesn't matter what wrapper it is. And so that's how I really think about the world. And we at Aristotle think about the world from a multi-sector lens.
turns.zh: 这么一来，它突然就只是一只债券而已，对吧？外壳是什么根本不重要。这就是我真正看待这个世界的方式，而我们在 Aristotle，是从多板块的视角来看世界的。

turns.en: And so it's not just about investment grade or non-investment grade. It's also CMBS or CLOs will have a very different risk return profile for the same rating versus corporates, for instance.
turns.zh: 所以这不只关乎投资级还是非投资级。同样是某个评级，CMBS 或 CLO 相比比如公司债，会有非常不同的风险回报特征。

turns.en: And so it's really quite a flexible product in terms of following that relative value. But what I will say is we're very cognizant of the risk that we're taking on.
turns.zh: 所以在追随相对价值这一点上，它确实是一个相当灵活的产品。但我要说的是，我们对自己承担的风险非常清楚。

turns.en: And that's, to me, what a benchmark does serve is it's not a benchmark of returns, per se, and it's absolutely not a benchmark of duration or asset class allocation.
turns.zh: 而在我看来，基准（benchmark）真正起的作用在于：它本身并不是一个回报的基准，更绝对不是一个久期或资产类别配置的基准。

turns.en: It's how much risk am I willing to take into the portfolio? Because that's how I think an investor should think about a benchmark of you're giving a client or you're giving a manager the freedom and flexibility to go pursue an outcome, but they have to stay within a predefined level of risk in order to achieve that outcome.
turns.zh: 它衡量的是：我愿意往组合里承担多少风险？因为我觉得投资者就应该这样来看基准——你给客户、给经理追求某个结果的自由和灵活性，但为了实现那个结果，他们必须待在一个预先设定好的风险水平之内。

turns.en: Because if I give you treasury like returns and equity like volatility, well, I've not done my job as a fixed income manager. So still a very keen eye on risk, but recognizing relative value ebbs and flows throughout the market and cycle.
turns.zh: 因为如果我给你国债那样的回报、却有股票那样的波动，那我这固定收益经理就没尽到职责。所以我们对风险始终盯得很紧，同时也认识到，相对价值会在整个市场和周期里此消彼长。

turns.en: So let's talk about the third one, Esther, as you called it, the short term income ETF. This is obviously, you know, you're more defensive, short duration play.
turns.zh: 那我们来聊聊第三只——你所说的 SDUR，也就是短期收益 ETF。这显然是一个更偏防御、短久期（short duration）的打法。

turns.en: I guess my curiosity would lie of what's the case for actually using active management in short duration and these such defensive, hopefully low volatility securities?
turns.zh: 我好奇的是：在短久期、这类偏防御、希望是低波动的证券里，用主动管理（active management）的理由到底是什么？

turns.en: I would say it's the same thing, right? It's recognizing that if you think about the world from a fixed income in just two broad levers, which is what most people would think about the world of fixed income in, you can pull an interest rate lever.
turns.zh: 我会说，道理是一样的，对吧？就是要认识到：如果你只用两个大杠杆来看固定收益这个世界——大多数人就是这么看固定收益的——你可以拉一个利率杠杆。

turns.en: You can bet on where the level of the Fed is going to move, the level of the front end part of the curve, two year treasuries versus 30 year treasuries.
turns.zh: 你可以押注美联储的利率水平会往哪里走、押注曲线前端（front end）的水平、两年期国债对三十年期国债。

turns.en: It's very much a topic that we're talking about right now, just given deficits and curve steepening, or you can pull a credit lever. You can say, well, I want to invest in very high quality companies or less quality companies, but the world is more nuanced than that and we've covered some of that, but the way I would think about short duration is it's for a client that doesn't want that interest rate risk.
turns.zh: 考虑到财政赤字和曲线变陡（curve steepening），这正是我们现在热议的话题。或者你也可以拉一个信用杠杆：你可以说，我想投非常高质量的公司，或者质量差一些的公司。但这个世界比这更细致，这些我们已经讲了一部分。而我看待短久期的方式是：它是为那些不想要利率风险的客户准备的。

turns.en: And so the biggest benefit of interest rate risk is it tends to go in the opposite direction of credit risk and we've emerged from a world where that has not been the case over the last three to five years.
turns.zh: 利率风险最大的好处在于，它往往和信用风险朝相反方向走，而我们刚刚走出的这个世界——在过去三到五年里——情况恰恰并非如此。

turns.en: But we have to remember the starting point was we started from a Fed that was pinned at zero because we were in a disinflationary environment and today we're in an inflationary environment.
turns.zh: 但我们必须记住，起点是：我们是从一个把利率死死钉在零的美联储出发的，因为当时我们处在通缩（disinflationary）环境里，而今天我们处在通胀环境里。

turns.en: So we won't go too far down that rabbit hole unless you want to. But the biggest benefit I think for a product like short duration is you're stripping out a lot of that potential interest rate exposure, which means you're stripping out a lot of that potential volatility, but you are still earning well in excess of what a low interest rate treasury would give you.
turns.zh: 除非你想深挖，否则我们就不往那个兔子洞里钻太深了。但我认为，像短久期这样的产品，最大的好处是：你剔除了大量潜在的利率敞口，也就意味着剔除了大量潜在的波动，可你赚到的仍然远超一只低利率敏感度的国债所能给你的。

turns.en: A low interest rate sensitive treasury would give you. So that product today is yielding about 5%, versus the front end of the treasury curve is well below that level and most clients for a very safe investment would be hard pressed to get much above four.
turns.zh: 也就是说，一只低利率敏感度的国债能给你的就那么多。所以这只产品今天的收益率大约在 5%，而国债曲线的前端远低于这个水平；对大多数客户来说，想要一项非常安全的投资，很难拿到明显高于 4% 的收益。

turns.en: Well, I actually do want to get into your macro read here in a second, but just curious, the active fixed income area in ETFs has been one of the fastest growing segments of the ETF industry.
turns.zh: 嗯，其实我一会儿确实想听听你的宏观判断，不过先好奇问一下：ETF 里的主动固定收益这一块，一直是整个 ETF 行业增长最快的细分领域之一。

turns.en: So what is driving that shift and how much runway do you think it still has? I think ETFs are easier to access. I think for many clients, they like that if they just go on their brokerage account, once an ETF is up and running, it's really broadly available in most places.
turns.zh: 那么是什么在推动这种转变？你觉得它还有多大的增长空间？我认为 ETF 更容易触达。对很多客户来说，他们喜欢的是：只要登录自己的券商账户，一旦某只 ETF 上线运行，它在大多数地方都能非常普遍地买到。

turns.en: As where mutual funds are a little bit different, right? Mutual funds might be available on one platform and not another. And so the sales process right along with it is a little bit different.
turns.zh: 而共同基金就有点不一样了，对吧？共同基金可能在一个平台上有、在另一个平台上却没有。所以随之而来的销售流程也会有些不同。

turns.en: I will say the ETF wrapper itself has a lot of advantages. It has some disadvantages, but those advantages are much more applicable to the world of equity securities, where you truly do generate capital gains and capital losses, and it just has a different tax regime than a mutual fund would.
turns.zh: 我得说，ETF 这个外壳本身有很多优势，也有一些劣势，但那些优势更适用于股票证券的世界——在那里你确实会产生资本利得和资本损失，而它的税收机制（tax regime）跟共同基金就是不一样。

turns.en: And so as you start applying it to the world of fixed income, I think it gets very nuanced very quickly. To me, the biggest benefit is the ability to transact with in-kind security.
turns.zh: 所以当你开始把它应用到固定收益世界时，我觉得情况很快就会变得非常微妙。对我来说，最大的好处是能够用实物证券（in-kind）来做交易。

turns.en: So I'm not having to buy something to sell something. It can just be a swap of cash for securities. And so, again, it's a little bit more efficient.
turns.zh: 也就是说，我不必为了卖一样东西而先买一样东西，它可以直接是现金和证券之间的互换。所以，同样地，它会更高效一些。

turns.en: But I think the reason why we've seen such a big rise is because it's really caught on in the world of equities, where it really does have some truly tremendous advantages to the product itself.
turns.zh: 但我认为，我们之所以看到它大幅崛起，是因为它在股票世界里真的火了起来——在那里，它对产品本身确实有一些极其巨大的优势。

turns.en: And then as clients have gotten comfortable with an ETF wrapper, they just want a lot of their other products to be in that wrapper as well.
turns.zh: 然后，随着客户对 ETF 这个外壳越来越习惯，他们就希望自己很多其他产品也用这个外壳来装。

turns.en: So I do want your macro read, right? Inflation is still elevated. You know, rates and yields are back in the news. Where do you see this? I'm not going to hold you to this, so don't worry.
turns.zh: 那我确实想听听你的宏观判断，对吧？通胀仍然偏高，你知道，利率和收益率又回到了新闻头条。你怎么看？我不会拿这个来‘锁死’你的，别担心。

turns.en: Where do you see rates going from here and how's that shaping how you guys are positioned in all of your products? Yeah. Well, whenever I kind of get that rates question, I always want to back up just a second and remind myself, this is really for myself, to remind myself that the world has changed and it's changed tremendously.
turns.zh: 你觉得接下来利率会往哪儿走？这又如何影响你们在所有产品上的仓位布局？嗯，每当被问到利率这个问题，我总是想先退一步提醒自己——这其实是对我自己说的——提醒自己世界已经变了，而且变化巨大。

turns.en: And it's because we as investors, for most people that are actively investing in their career today or saving as savers, most of us have existed in a world that is not normal.
turns.zh: 这是因为，作为投资者——对今天大多数在职业生涯里积极投资、或者作为储蓄者存钱的人来说——我们大多数人都生活在一个并不正常的世界里。

turns.en: And that is a world where interest rates were artificially pinned very low and for good reason, because they were trying to increase demand, what central banks were trying to do in the context of price stability, of keeping inflation in check, was actually to push the level of inflation up towards their target of 2% is what most central banks say.
turns.zh: 在那个世界里，利率被人为地死死压在很低的水平，而且是有充分理由的：因为他们想刺激需求。在物价稳定、控制通胀这个框架下，各家央行想做的，其实是把通胀水平往上推，推向多数央行所说的 2% 的目标。

turns.en: And that's not the normal state of the world, but it's the normal state of the world for most of us and our financial history. And that world is now no longer the case, right?
turns.zh: 这并不是世界的常态，但对我们大多数人以及我们的金融经历来说，它却是常态。而那个世界现在已经不复存在了，对吧？

turns.en: Today, inflation is too high. We're trying to pull it down. It's been too high for five plus years. And I think that sets up a very nuanced picture for answering the question of where interest rates are going to go, right?
turns.zh: 今天，通胀太高了，我们正试图把它压下来。它已经太高五年多了。我认为，这就为回答‘利率会往哪儿走’这个问题，铺陈出一幅非常微妙的图景，对吧？

turns.en: Today, we have an environment where inflation is too high and it's been too high for two long, five years. And I think this Fed is much like we've transitioned from that world of low inflation to high inflation.
turns.zh: 今天，我们处在一个通胀过高、而且已经过高太久——五年了——的环境里。我认为这一届美联储很像是：我们已经从那个低通胀的世界，过渡到了高通胀的世界。

turns.en: The new Fed share is also doing the same thing, right? The old Fed share took over a world of low inflation, exited a world of high inflation, this Fed share wash has come in and all he has to contend with is a world of high inflation.
turns.zh: 新任美联储主席也在经历同样的转变，对吧？上一任美联储主席接手的是一个低通胀的世界，卸任时是一个高通胀的世界；而这一任美联储主席 Warsh 上任，他要应对的完完全全就是一个高通胀的世界。

turns.en: And so I think the reaction function is likely to be very different. But importantly, we've also moved from this mentality of, well, high inflation is transitory, right?
turns.zh: 所以我认为，他的反应函数（reaction function）很可能会非常不同。但更重要的是，我们也已经摆脱了那种‘高通胀只是暂时的（transitory）’的心态，对吧？

turns.en: First, we had a COVID shock. Who can blame the world for that, right? We had a supply chain disruption. Then we had the reopening trade. Then we had low interest rates and housing that moved into the prices of rents and all sorts of things.
turns.zh: 一开始，我们有一场新冠冲击——这谁能怪世界呢，对吧？我们经历了供应链中断，然后是重启交易（reopening trade），接着是低利率和住房，这些又传导进了房租价格等等各种东西里。

turns.en: And now maybe we have an oil shock or memory shock because of AI. And this Fed share, I think is correctly looking at the world and being like, well, if we have one shock after the other, eventually it's not a shock.
turns.zh: 而现在，也许我们又有了石油冲击，或者因为 AI 而起的存储（memory）冲击。我认为这一任美联储主席看世界的方式是对的：如果我们一个冲击接着一个冲击，那最终它就不算冲击了。

turns.en: It's just the world that we live in. And I make a joke, right? Every year on December 31st, I'm going to be more healthy. I'm going to go to the gym and something changes in the world.
turns.zh: 它只是我们生活的这个世界本来的样子。我打个比方，对吧？每年 12 月 31 日，我都会说：我要更健康，我要去健身房。然后世界里就冒出点什么事。

turns.en: My friend has a party or a birthday or something and I eat dessert and then, oh, it's really nice and I don't want to go to the gym today. And eventually it just becomes my state of affairs for the rest of the year.
turns.zh: 朋友办个派对、过个生日什么的，我就吃了甜点，然后心想：哎呀真好吃，今天不想去健身房了。就这样，它最终变成了我这一年剩下时间里的常态。

turns.en: I'm not quite as healthy as I want. And so I think this Fed share is much more willing to pull that interest rate lever because really what it translates to do is we have too much demand chasing too few goods.
turns.zh: 结果我没变得像自己想的那样健康。所以我认为，这一任美联储主席更愿意去拉动利率那个杠杆，因为它真正意味着的是：我们有太多的需求在追逐太少的商品。

turns.en: And it's hard. It's a tough pill to swallow, but we need less demand. And so I think the immediate direction of interest rates is higher from here.
turns.zh: 这很难，是一剂难以下咽的苦药，但我们需要更少的需求。所以我认为，利率眼下的方向是从这里往上走。

turns.en: I do think this Fed will ultimately acquiesce and raise rates, but I think that's the medicine and the ultimate cure is that inflation comes down.
turns.zh: 我确实认为这届美联储最终会认了、会加息，但我觉得那是药，而最终的解药，是通胀降下来。

turns.en: And so over the medium term, I think interest rates are headed lower. And I think that that's a really tremendous opportunity in the world of fixed income today.
turns.zh: 所以从中期来看，我认为利率会往下走。而且我觉得，这在今天的固定收益世界里，是一个真正巨大的机会。

turns.en: So we are a little bit above duration. And the first question I get is, well, why are you above weight duration? If you think interest rates are moving higher?
turns.zh: 所以我们的久期是略微超配的。别人问我的第一个问题就是：既然你觉得利率会往上走，为什么还要超配久期？

turns.en: And the biggest answer and reason that I believe that is because they're an excellent hedge to some of that credit exposure. And so interest rates are probably moving a little bit higher, but today we exist in a world where everyone is stretched.
turns.zh: 而我这么做的最大理由和答案是：久期是对那部分信用敞口的一个绝佳对冲（hedge）。所以利率可能会略微走高，但今天我们所处的这个世界里，每个人都被绷得很紧。

turns.en: I think when we're talking, right, everyone on the other side of this, myself, everybody, we all feel that pinch of higher interest rates, higher gas prices, higher food prices, everything costs more.
turns.zh: 我想，就在我们说话的这会儿，对吧，这其中的每一个人——我自己、所有人——都感受到了那种挤压：更高的利率、更贵的油价、更贵的食品价格，什么都更贵了。

turns.en: And so it doesn't take that much higher level of interest rates to see that demand function pull back. And in that world, you'd see credit spreads widen.
turns.zh: 所以，利率不需要再高多少，就能看到那个需求函数往回缩。而在那样的世界里，你会看到信用利差（credit spreads）走阔。

turns.en: So ultimately, I like the hedge of that. And really what I like is, again, what is the outcome that we're trying to achieve, a lower volatility instrument that clients can use in concert with equities and other things.
turns.zh: 所以归根结底，我喜欢它带来的那份对冲。而我真正喜欢的，还是那句话：我们想达成的结果是什么？——一个波动更低的工具，让客户可以把它和股票以及其他东西搭配着用。

turns.en: So I really want to focus on that downside protection because I do think interest rates are moving lower over time and the direction is certainly down from here.
turns.zh: 所以我真的很想聚焦在那份下行保护（downside protection）上，因为我确实认为利率会随时间往下走，方向肯定是从这里向下。

turns.en: So, you know, last question, million dollar question, you kind of briefly answered it, was, you know, you've got these three ETFs. How would you tell an advisor who's already got an existing diversified model portfolio, how would you recommend they kind of use them in their practice or where would you put them?
turns.zh: 那么，你知道，最后一个问题，一个价值百万美元的问题，你其实已经简略回答过了：你有这三只 ETF，你会怎么告诉一个已经有一套现成的、分散化模型组合（model portfolio）的投顾——你会建议他们在实务中怎么使用这些 ETF，或者说你会把它们放在组合的什么位置？

turns.en: Yeah, to me, again, the most important question is, what are you trying to do and what do you have that's trying to do that? And so one of the things I really have loved about my investing career and one of the things I really love about being here at Aristotle Pacific is the way that we generate returns is almost certainly going to be very different than the way that many other folks are attempting to generate returns.
turns.zh: 嗯，对我来说，最重要的问题还是：你想达成什么？你现在手上有什么在帮你达成它？在我的投资生涯里，有一件事我特别喜欢，也是我在 Aristotle Pacific 特别看重的一点——那就是我们创造回报的方式，几乎注定会和很多其他人试图创造回报的方式非常不同。

turns.en: And so if nothing else, it's very complimentary, right? Not all things work at all times. And I would say that about ourselves. And I would certainly say it about anybody else, but it's you want a little bit of things that will zig when the other zags.
turns.zh: 所以别的不说，它是极具互补性（complementary）的，对吧？没有东西能在所有时候都奏效——这话我说我们自己适用，说任何其他人也绝对适用。你要的是那种‘当别人往左、它往右’的东西，各配一点。

turns.en: And so I would say really get to know the outcome that your manager is after the outcomes that we are after and how we're going to generate those returns and then where it potentially pairs well.
turns.zh: 所以我会说，真正去了解你的经理所追求的结果、我们所追求的那些结果，以及我们打算怎么创造这些回报，然后再看它可能和什么搭配得好。

turns.en: You know, to give you maybe a more succinct answer, you brought up PIMCO, partly because it's my background. Generally, they're going to invest from the top down.
turns.zh: 你知道，也许给你一个更简洁的回答：你提到了 PIMCO，部分也是因为那是我的老东家背景。一般来说，他们是从自上而下去投资的。

turns.en: And so again, that's fine, but we're going to do things very differently. And so I think we're a very good compliment to some of those larger managers that take a much stronger macro view within their portfolios and they will win and lose by that, we aren't going to win and lose by the macro view.
turns.zh: 同样，那样也没问题，但我们要做的事情会非常不一样。所以我认为，对于那些在组合里采取更强宏观观点的大型管理人来说，我们是一个很好的互补——他们会因宏观观点而成、因宏观观点而败，而我们不会因宏观观点而成败。

turns.en: And so if nothing else, it's a pretty interesting compliment to many of the larger players out there that really, just because of their size, have to take a broad macro view instead of individual credits.
turns.zh: 所以别的不说，对市面上很多大型玩家而言，我们是一个相当有意思的互补——他们纯粹因为体量的原因，不得不采取一种宽泛的宏观视角，而不是去研究一个个具体的信用主体。

turns.en: And are you being paid to take that risk and then where on the relative value spectrum, Jeff, I really appreciate you taking some time with me today.
turns.zh: 以及，你承担那份风险到底有没有得到相应的补偿，还有在相对价值谱系上你处在哪个位置。Jeff，真的很感谢你今天抽出时间跟我聊。

turns.en: Before I let you go, where can people learn more about Aristotle and these sweet, your suite of new three new ETFs? Yeah, absolutely. Welcome to visit our websites where Aristotle Pacific.com as well as AristotleFunds.com will both have those resources.
turns.zh: 在放你走之前，大家可以在哪里更多地了解 Aristotle，以及你这一整套三只新 ETF？当然可以。欢迎访问我们的网站，AristotlePacific.com 和 AristotleFunds.com 上都会有这些资料。

turns.en: And then I'm trying post pretty regularly on LinkedIn. And so if folks want to follow me there, that's where you can find me for some of those macro insights.
turns.zh: 然后我也在尽量比较规律地在 LinkedIn 上发帖。所以如果大家想在那儿关注我、想看我的一些宏观见解，就能在那里找到我。

turns.en: Again, Jeff, thanks again for hanging out with me. Yeah, absolutely. Great conversation. Thank you.
turns.zh: 再次谢谢你，Jeff，感谢你来跟我聊。好啊，当然，这是一次很棒的对话，谢谢你。
